A1.justification: The PDFs describe the same substantially revised work, with identifiable continuity in weighted clique expansion, mathematical arguments and benchmarks. v1 includes Appendices A–I. v2 ends at the references despite repeatedly referring to an appendix for proofs and experimental details, limiting comparison of that supporting material.

before.justification: v1 reports original WCE-GNN classification results on nine datasets, alongside architecture ablations, depth studies and computational-efficiency experiments in Section 6.

after.justification: v2 reports original SHNN classification results, component ablations and hyperlink-prediction experiments. Section 6.1 explicitly identifies the hyperlink-prediction results as experiments conducted by the authors.

M1.justification: v1 trains GCNII-based WCE-GNN propagation layers jointly with an MLP classifier. v2 replaces this with fixed polynomial propagation, SX_V, computed before training, and trains only the downstream prediction model. Learnable propagation matrices and nonlinearities are eliminated. The hyperedge-size weights and normalization are retained, but the actual learning procedure changes substantially.

E1.justification: Node-classification coverage contracts from nine datasets to six: Cora, Pubmed and Walmart are omitted, while the other six remain. v2 adds hyperlink prediction on Cora-CA, Citeseer and House, introducing a distinct task beyond the node classification evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: The node-classification comparison adds HNHN and Deep-HGNN and removes SheafHyperGNN. UniGCNII matches the earlier UniGNN implementation described in v1 Appendix B and is not a new comparator. The ablation comparisons also change substantially: v1 evaluates GAT, SGC and GCN alternatives, whereas v2 uses a pure MLP and SHNN component controls.

E3.justification: The node-classification split remains 50%/25%/25%. The new hyperlink protocol specifies the same split proportions, five fake hyperedges per real hyperedge, message passing using real training and validation hyperedges, and AUC evaluation. Efficiency measurement changes from seconds per epoch averaged over 100 training-and-validation epochs to relative training time required to reach optimal performance; these timings are not directly comparable.

E4.justification: v1 studies cross-model depth sensitivity and memory/runtime scaling, and crosses four GNN architectures with weighted or unweighted clique expansion. v2 instead studies SHNN depth jointly with alpha and compares a pure MLP, unweighted SHNN and weighted SHNN. The weighting question persists, but the architecture, propagation and oversmoothing controls are substantially redesigned.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten node-classification runs and display results with ± quantities and depth-study error bars. v1 explicitly identifies standard deviations; v2 does not define the dispersion quantities or state repetition counts for hyperlink prediction. With the referenced v2 appendix unavailable, changes to the full uncertainty-reporting procedure cannot be established reliably.

E6.justification: v2 replaces the proposed-model results and adds hyperlink AUC, relative training-time and new ablation findings. For example, Cora-CA accuracy is 86.25 ± 1.25 for WCE-GNN in v1 and 86.54 ± 1.32 for SHNN in v2; these concern different models. AllSetTransformer's House/Senate scores change from 69.33/51.83 to 51.83/69.33 without explanation. The dataset tables also interchange their House/Senate homophily values.

T1.justification: The main theoretical program changes from input-space equivalence, shared inductive bias and spectral expressivity to HNN simplification, L-hop propagation support, entropy equality and SHNN convergence. Some polynomial and regularized-smoothing arguments already appear in v1 Appendix E and are adapted rather than entirely new. Nevertheless, v2's Lemma 3.2 and Proposition 4.1 introduce materially different formal statements. Its referenced full proofs are unavailable.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from showing that a GNN on a weighted clique expansion can approximate HyperGNNs for node classification to introducing a training-free feature generator for multiple downstream tasks. The abstract replaces the emphasis on superior classification accuracy and memory/runtime efficiency with competitive performance, reduced training complexity, information utilization and oversmoothing resistance.

C2.justification: v2 newly explains smaller hyperlink-prediction speedups through the greater cost of its prediction head and interprets alpha sensitivity as showing particular benefits from preserving individual features on heterophilic datasets. The stated limitation changes from lacking hyperlink-prediction evaluation to lacking hypergraph-level evaluation. v1's concluding questions about whether node classification needs higher-order interactions are no longer presented.

D1.justification: v1 states that WCE-GNN code and data are available through GitHub; v2 announces a prospective anonymous SHNN code release with running commands. v2 also identifies the DeepSets implementation used for hyperlink prediction and clarifies which baseline accuracies are reused or newly measured. PyTorch and RTX 3090 remain unchanged. Additional hyperparameter disclosures cannot be checked because the referenced appendix is absent.

R1.justification: Research positioning changes from bridging graph and hypergraph learning, particularly relative to Agarwal et al., to reducing training costs through ideas from SIGN and SGC. v2 adds substantive comparisons with LightHGNN and Hypergraph-MLP, distinguishing their inference-efficiency objectives from its training-efficiency objective. This substantially revises the related-work argument.

P1.justification: The title changes from Hypergraph Node Classification With Graph Neural Networks to Simplifying Hypergraph Neural Networks. The abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The organization changes from preliminary material followed by theory and the practical framework to notation, methodology and subsequent analysis, with substantially revised terminology and narrative.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn as a two-pipeline training comparison. The earlier depth, memory and per-epoch runtime displays are replaced by relative-time bars, hyperlink AUC/time plots and alpha-depth plots. Tables gain a model-formulation overview, dataset semantics, average-accuracy columns and ranking marks; the ablation table becomes a component-presence comparison. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's stated lack of hyperlink-prediction evidence and adds useful propagation and alpha controls for the revised model. However, node-classification coverage narrows, unexplained table-value swaps weaken reporting reliability, and important new proofs and settings depend on an appendix absent from the supplied PDF, whereas v1 supplies extensive proofs. These benefits and limitations do not support a reliable net judgment of overall quality improvement.
